sec: Anatomical relations, cavernous sinus and pituitary MRI

items.q: Which anatomical structure lies immediately posterior and inferior to the sella turcica, providing the standard surgical corridor for pituitary adenomas?
items.exp: The sphenoid sinus lies posterior/inferior to the sella and allows the transsphenoidal surgical approach. (Book p939)

items.q: The dural reflection forming the roof of the hypophyseal fossa is the ___; injury to it can cause CSF rhinorrhea and empty sella syndrome.
items.exp: The diaphragma sellae forms the dural roof of the sella; injury leads to CSF leaks and empty sella syndrome. (Book p939)

items.q: A 45-year-old male with a large pituitary macroadenoma expanding laterally into the cavernous sinus presents with acute diplopia and isolated left lateral rectus palsy. Which cranial nerve is involved first?
items.exp: Lateral expansion of a pituitary tumor into the cavernous sinus involves the sixth cranial nerve (abducent nerve) first, causing lateral rectus palsy. (Book p939)

items.q: Which neural or vascular structure does NOT traverse the cavernous sinus adjacent to the pituitary fossa?
items.exp: The cavernous sinus contains the internal carotid artery, CN III, CN IV, CN VI, V1, and V2; V3 passes through the foramen ovale outside the sinus. (Book p939)

items.q: Match the sellar boundary to its primary related structure — 1) Lateral relation 2) Inferior/posterior approach 3) Ventral/superior dural roof … A) Cavernous sinus B) Sphenoid sinus C) Diaphragma sellae
items.exp: The cavernous sinus lies laterally, the sphenoid sinus lies inferiorly/posteriorly, and the diaphragma sellae forms the roof. (Book p939)

items.q: On non-contrast T1-weighted coronal and sagittal MRI, the normal pituitary gland appears:
items.exp: On T1 MRI (coronal, sagittal, and without contrast), the normal pituitary appears isointense. (Book p939)

items.q: Assess the contrast enhancement patterns of the pituitary gland: I The normal pituitary demonstrates uniform avid gadolinium enhancement. II A pituitary microadenoma typically exhibits delayed or non-uniform enhancement due to lower capillary vascularity.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Normal pituitary shows uniform contrast uptake, whereas adenomas demonstrate less vascularity and do not take up contrast uniformly. (Book p939)

items.q: A neuroradiologist evaluates a sagittal T1 MRI of a 22-year-old male with severe polyuria and polydipsia. Absence of the normal hyperintense posterior pituitary 'bright spot' is diagnostic of:
items.exp: Absence of the normal posterior pituitary T1 bright spot is diagnostic of central diabetes insipidus in 80% of cases. (Book p939)

items.q: The normal T1-weighted sagittal MRI 'bright spot' in the posterior sella represents stored vasopressin-neurophysin granules in the ___ pituitary.
items.exp: The normal bright spot on sagittal T1 MRI represents stored neurosecretory granules in the posterior pituitary. (Book p939)

items.q: Match the MRI appearance on T1 imaging to the pathological condition — 1) Normal posterior lobe bright spot absent 2) Hypoenhancing focal sellar lesion 3) Diffuse uniform gadolinium uptake … A) Central diabetes insipidus (80%) B) Pituitary adenoma C) Normal anterior pituitary gland
items.exp: Absence of bright spot indicates central DI; focal hypoenhancement indicates adenoma; uniform contrast uptake indicates normal gland. (Book p939)

items.q: Which trigeminal nerve divisions traverse the cavernous sinus along its lateral dural wall?
items.exp: The lateral wall of the cavernous sinus contains the ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) divisions of the trigeminal nerve. (Book p939)

items.q: Assess the clinical implications of diaphragmatic injury: I A tear in the diaphragma sellae can cause CSF leakage. II Chronic CSF pressure through the defect can lead to empty sella syndrome.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Injury to the diaphragma sellae permits CSF leakage and can progress to empty sella syndrome. (Book p939)
